brief: August headline CPI rose 0.4% MoM and 3.4% YoY, both in line with expectations. Core CPI rose 0.3% MoM (0.29%), above the 0.2% consensus, driven by services ex housing; annual core still eased from 2.5% to 2.4%, which the note says falls short of a renewed inflation breakout. Gasoline (+3.9% MoM) drove over a third of the headline move, while core services ex housing rose 0.51% MoM, the strongest since January and up 3.0% YoY; soft rent and OER (+0.2% each) held the aggregate core down, a drag the note calls mechanical rather than a sign inflation pressure is moderating. Combined with last week's payroll rebound, this leaves the Fed facing a tightening labor market alongside above-target inflation, strengthening the case for a hike next week. In year-on-year terms disinflation has stalled, so the Fed SHOULD hike; the note also argues there is a strategic reason to hike regardless of the CPI print, to back up Fed Chair Warsh's inflation-fighting credibility, especially since investors doubt he can move before the midterms, so what Warsh should do and what he will do may now be aligned.
